permanent_fix_required: Extract a shared migration helper (e.g. addColumnWithIndex) and have each service-level migration call it instead of inlining the boilerplate. The helper enforces the contract; individual migrations stop drifting.
root_cause_summary: TypeORM migration generator copies the add-column-then-index boilerplate verbatim into each new migration file. There is no shared helper, so the pattern multiplies across services and silently absorbs maintenance cost.

short_term_action_taken.rationale: The originating finding (F-001) acts as a tracked regression marker. Future migrations that add a fourth instance should surface against this finding so the duplication count stays auditable.

resolution_summary: addColumnWithIndex (+ dropColumnWithIndex) landed in libs/backend-common/src/database/migration-helpers.ts: both halves guarded, identifiers validated through validateSqlIdentifier, unqualified DDL by default (tenant search_path routing) with an explicit schema for MODULE_SCHEMAS infrastructure tables. Shipped migrations are immutable and stay untouched; the new invariant tests/invariants/migration-column-index-pair.spec.ts bans FUTURE same-table inlined pairs (comment-stripped, up()-body-scoped, per-table correlation) with an in-spec grandfather allowlist of the 4 sensor-service instances and a stale-exemption test. Honesty note: the original short_term_action_taken referenced aria-findings/F-001.json as a regression marker, but aria-findings/ is empty on this tree — the dangling reference is recorded here rather than papered over; the pair invariant is the enforcement that replaces it.
